content: This medication should be discarded properly when it is expired or no longer needed. The information provided here was last revised in May 2024. Important Usage Information: This document is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific condition. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, headache, or temporary hair loss. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a comprehensive list of side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before taking albendazole, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other benzimidazole anthelmintic drugs (e.g., mebendazole), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Albendazole may cause liver problems. Limit alcohol consumption while using this medication, as alcohol increases the risk of liver complications. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Avoid becoming pregnant while using albendazole, as it may harm an unborn baby. Your doctor should order a pregnancy test before starting this medication. Use reliable birth control methods during treatment and for three days after the last dose. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Usage and Monitoring: This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., liver function tests, complete blood counts) should be conducted before starting this medication and during its use. Attend all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Additional Notes: This information is provided for general informational and educational purposes only. Individual plans may vary, and formulary information is subject to change. Contact the applicable plan provider for the most current information.
